messages:
priya-g: Hi team — quick tax situation. I was on a J-1 visa through 2025-06-15 (DS-2019 on file) and changed to H-1B with HR on 2025-06-20. My June/July paystubs show federal income tax withheld and FICA taken. Should I expect a W-2 or 1042-S for 2025? I think part-year treaty/exemption might apply.

jen-people-ops: @priya-g thanks for the heads-up. Can you attach DS-2019, I-797, and the date HR recorded the status change? Well loop payroll/tax to confirm. :mag: 

priya-g: Attached DS-2019 and I-797 in the ticket PR-2026-010 (docs: DS2019.pdf, I797.pdf). HR shows status change effective 2025-06-20.

payroll-bot: Created ticket PR-2026-010: "Visa status midyear & correct tax form (W-2 vs 1042-S) - priya-g" assigned to samir-payroll.

samir-payroll: Thanks. Quick primer: J-1 nonresident scholars/students can be exempt from FICA and may have treaty claims; wages paid while treaty/exempt sometimes appear on 1042-S instead of W-2. But if you became resident for tax purposes or were payrolled as an employee post-change, payroll may have issued wages on W-2. Need to verify pay period dates and the paystub tax codes.

tax-counsel: Hi @samir-payroll @priya-g — we'll review the immigration docs and days present. Two possible outcomes: (1) Part-year 1042-S for the J-1-exempt wages + W-2 for H-1B/resident wages, or (2) W-2 for all wages and payroll issues a W-2c/adjustment if withholding was incorrect. Well confirm treaty article applicability and whether Form 8233 or other withholding exemption forms were used.

steph-mgr: I can confirm priyas assignment dates and that relocation paperwork matches. Happy to add manager attestation to the ticket. :white_check_mark:

priya-g: Appreciate it. Whats the usual timeline? I file taxes with a CPA and want to give them heads-up.

samir-payroll: We aim to complete the initial review in ~10 business days after docs are verified. If a corrected form is needed (W-2c or amended 1042-S), that can take additional processing time and may impact payroll/QB schedules. If refunds are due for FICA incorrectly withheld, we typically: 1) refund on a payroll run if within our refund window, or 2) provide documentation so employee can claim a refund on their return; for FICA there are specific IRS procedures if we cannot refund directly.

priya-g: Noted. Can you confirm which pay periods are considered "J-1 wages" vs "H-1B wages"? My June pay period straddles the change (pay date 2025-06-27 for work through 2025-06-15).

samir-payroll: Good question. We classify by work dates in the payroll period, not pay date. So if your earnings were for work through 6/15, those will be treated based on your J-1 status. Well extract line-item earnings from the payroll ledger and mark periods. Example extract (internal):

```
2025-06-01 to 2025-06-15  => J-1 status => possible exemption
2025-06-16 to 2025-06-30  => H-1B status => standard withholding
```

samir-payroll: I'll paste the ledger lines to the ticket once pulled. If FICA was withheld on the J-1 portion, we'll evaluate refund vs documentation.

jen-people-ops: Action list: priya - confirm docs uploaded (done); steph - manager attestation in PR-2026-010; samir/tax-counsel - review and post proposed forms (W-2, W-2c, or 1042-S) and timeline. I'll follow up EOW. :calendar: 

priya-g: Manager attestation added. Thanks everyone.

tax-counsel: One more note for priya: if a 1042-S is issued for scholarship or fellowship income types, the box descriptions differ from W-2. Example snippet for reference (illustrative only):

```
Box 1: Gross income subject to tax treaty
Box 2: Amount exempted by treaty
Box 15: Withholding agent EIN
```

tax-counsel: We'll confirm exact box mapping and whether a dual-form approach is necessary. If youre working with a CPA, cc them on the ticket so we can coordinate withholding docs.

jen-people-ops: Thanks team. Marking thread as tracked and will post final resolution here once payroll/tax complete. :raised_hands:
